subject: negative binomial N-mixture model in BUGS

messages.author: 39971e2c19b8ec70
messages.subject: negative binomial N-mixture model in BUGS
parts:
Hi everyone!

Is there a BUGS code available for N-mixture model with negative binomial
distribution for the lambda part instead of poisson (for overdispersed
data)? I.e. BUGS equivalent for unmarked::pcount(.., mixture = "NB")?

I've been looking into BPA, AHM1, papers of Marc, Linden, Chandler, Royle etc. but I
only found the ugly (sorry :-)) likelihood formulas and reparametrization..
it's certainly possible to build it from there but I much much prefer to see
if there is any working code first...

Thanks a lot!

Tomas

messages.author: 4a635fe980c8c1cd
messages.subject: Re: negative binomial N-mixture model in BUGS
parts:
Hi Tomas,

I think the BUGS/JAGS dnegbin is the less useful formulation of the distribution (a model for the number of failures occurring before a given # of successes), although STAN has a negbinomial_2 distribution that is the more useful lambda and overdispersion parameterization.  To my knowledge, the easiest way to incorporate over-dispersion in BUGS/JAGS is to include an additional error term ~ Normal(0, sigma), but I'd be curious to hear from others.

Cheers,

John

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: negative binomial N-mixture model in BUGS
parts:
Dear Tomas,

in the AHM1 book, there is an example of that more useful lambda/overdispersion parameterization of the dnegbin distribution function in BUGS, see comment on page 337 and then the actual analysis on page 507. I realize that neither is in the index though.....

John's suggestion of the Poisson-lognormal as an alternative to the NegBin is a good one of course.

Best regards  --  Marc
